content: An infobox on Wikipedia is a consistently formatted table or box that appears in articles with a shared subject. Its purpose is to provide summary information in a standardized manner across articles or to enhance navigation to closely related articles within the same subject area. An infobox can be considered a generalization of a taxobox, which is specifically used to summarize information about an organism or a group of organisms. If you create an infobox for a new project, it should first be proposed on the Wikipedia: List of infoboxes/Proposed sub-page. Once implemented, it should be moved to the appropriate sub-page of the main list. If you decide to use colors in your infobox, ensure that the color you choose is not already in use. Add your chosen color to the list of used colors so others are aware it has been taken. You can either use the same color for all tables within a project or adopt a system of color differentiation. For example, the organism taxobox uses distinct colors for each of the biological kingdoms. For more information on permissible colors, refer to the article on web colors. If you wish to redesign an infobox, you should consult the relevant WikiProject. An infobox may or may not utilize the template software feature. Infobox templates serve as an alternative to static infoboxes, allowing for a consistent appearance across subject items with minimal coding required within articles. For further details, refer to Wikipedia: Infobox templates. If your infobox is aligned to the right, it is recommended that its width does not exceed one-third of the available page width. The basic template pattern for an infobox can be found at Template: Infobox. This basic template includes the use of optional parameters, which can be compared to the conditional logic described in Wikipedia: Qif conditionals. For an example of a taxobox, refer to Wikipedia: WikiProject Tree of Life/taxobox usage, which provides comprehensive instructions.
